bottlenecks_identified: Recurring milestone-scoped timing-detector false-zero: 0 experiment commits attributed since activation of 2026.06.403, the same gap documented continuously across .363-.402. The detector cannot map commits to the active milestone window, so the retro has no wall-time profile and no slowest-experiment ranking to analyze.

No write-time duration_s / compute_bound stamping in the retro pipeline: even when artifacts exist on disk, there is no deterministic per-experiment duration for the retro to rank slowest tasks, so it falls back to hand-reading the changelog/disk every milestone.
Silent propagation: the detector returning 0 looks identical to a genuinely empty milestone, so the false-zero is only caught by manual on-disk cross-check rather than an automatic tripwire.
improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector: scan results/ artifact mtimes within the activation->close window AND fall back to the ops/changelog.md milestone window when git commit-attribution returns 0.

Stamp duration_s plus a compute_bound boolean at experiment write-time (in scripts/experiment_template.py build_result) so the retro can rank slowest tasks deterministically without re-deriving timing from git history.

Emit a detector_gap_suspected tripwire when the commit-based detector returns 0 but on-disk artifacts exist for the milestone window, converting the silent false-zero into a visible signal at retro time.
Keep the GPU-idle bottleneck gated on >=1 compute-bound task being present (correctly NOT flagged this milestone since gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null).
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector (mtime-window scan + ops/changelog.md milestone-window fallback) — this is the single recurring operational failure spanning .363-.403 and it blocks every operational retro's numeric analysis.
Add write-time duration_s + compute_bound stamping in build_result() so slowest-experiment ranking is deterministic and detector-independent.

Wire a detector_gap_suspected tripwire that fires when commit-attribution=0 yet on-disk artifacts exist, so a false-zero is surfaced automatically instead of propagating into the retro as a phantom empty milestone.
meta_reflection: The recurring failure mode this milestone is observability, not execution: per the retro's own authoritative timing detector there is no wall-time to optimize (0/0/null), and the GPU idleness is correct given 0 compute-bound tasks. The honest operational read is that the detector keeps reporting an empty milestone while on-disk ground truth (read this turn) shows .403 ran a full task slate and closed publication-ready — so the highest-leverage operational fix remains making timing self-evident at experiment write-time rather than re-deriving it by hand each retro.
